cells.tense: A structure that was keeping up a false shape is falling now because the ground under it was never there.
cells.act: do the small practice again, alone, today
cells.ask: Sit down today with the small thing you already practice, by yourself, and keep it the same length as the last time.
cells.core:
Something that rested on nothing solid is losing its grip, right where what was outside begins to come in. It is not a disaster. The false part goes, and the clearing can be walked through steadily.
A repeating practice is what keeps the hand steady while it goes. Sit down today with the small thing you already do, by yourself, and keep it short and ordinary. Same length as the last time. What tells you it is working is that the length stops mattering — you are there, you are doing it, and the doing is the point. A structure falls that needed to fall, and you are the one standing when it does.
cells.sheetLine: The structure is falling and your small practice keeps you steady
cells.verb: Break open a structure built on ground that was never there
cells.place: At the threshold where something that was outside is arriving now

cells.tense: Before anything can hold, you are already taking it apart, and the clearing runs in front of what is really here.
cells.act: keep the ritual and give it room to change
cells.ask: Keep the ritual you share with them and give it one room to change when it next happens.
cells.core:
At the threshold where something is arriving now, the clearing comes down before the arrival does. Structures are being taken apart before they have stood long enough to carry anything. From your side, it reads as freedom. From theirs, it reads as a room where nothing is permitted to last. What is thin here is contact, and more force will not fix it.
That is where the shared thing comes in. Keep one ritual with the people who keep it with you, and let one room open in it next time it is done. Teaching it with one change inside it lets a living thing stay alive instead of being cleared for the sin of being old. The table keeps something on it.
cells.sheetLine: You're clearing everything before anything has had a chance to stand.
cells.verb: Break open a structure built on ground that was never there

cells.tense: A structure that stopped holding is still being held up, and the moment it needed to come down has already passed.
cells.act: put a date, a place, a container on it
cells.ask: Put a date and a place on what you're holding up, in your own hand, and be there when it comes.
cells.core:
What is arriving now is already behind you. You are holding up a structure that stopped holding. The old shape still has its hours, the phrases still come out of habit, and the thing itself stopped carrying weight a while back. What gets spent on keeping it up is not available for whatever is next.
Structure is for making the next move possible, not for propping up the last one. Write a date and a place on the thing you are keeping up — one container, your own handwriting, not the shared calendar. Then be there. If it holds, it holds honestly. If it doesn't, the gap is right there, and something alive can go in it.

cells.tense: Something is about to fall in what you are building, and your own account has not caught up with it yet.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Take a step today toward something you want, small enough that you can point to it tonight.
cells.core:
At the threshold where something is entering now, part of what you are building is about to come down. You talk about it as ground you found, not ground you laid, and nothing in how you say it has shifted. The fall is not the missing piece. How you're describing it is.
Direction comes back through movement, not through more looking. Take a step today toward something you actually want — small enough that you can point to it tonight, and not necessarily the right step. The step will not hand you a plan. It will just show you where you are leaning. When the thing comes down, you will have been walking. That is what carries.
cells.sheetLine: Something's about to fall and you're not telling yourself.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: each cell's core tells the reader what is true of their one capacity in one part of their life, and a reader could reasonably say the card text does not claim that their exact situation is the one where a structure that cannot hold is going to fall. The ask survives being wrong in all four cells because in each case it is taken word for word from the medicine's own list of acts and made small in the seat, not built on a picture of the person's life or a promise about what the card will do. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person: 'Movement replaces keeping' — in the reducer's cell, 'One proper form, kept' relies on the same abstract cadence without naming a kept date or slot, which would be invisible.
